title: Upload response URL trusts request base URL
reasoning: The upload response constructs the artifact URL from request.base_url. In common ASGI deployments this value is influenced by Host and forwarded headers unless separately constrained by trusted proxy configuration. A malicious or misconfigured Host header can therefore cause the API to return an attacker-controlled absolute artifact URL, which is a response poisoning/phishing risk and can break clients that persist or display the returned URL.
recommendation: Build artifact URLs from a configured canonical backend/public base URL, or return a relative artifact path instead of an absolute URL. If proxy-derived hosts are required, enforce trusted host/proxy middleware and cover the expected behavior in tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included, and the visible response model only asserts a url field exists, not that it is derived from a trusted source.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test that sends a forged Host header during upload and asserts the returned url uses the configured canonical base URL or a relative /api/artifacts/{id} path.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/routes/artifacts/router.py, configuration or API contract if a canonical base URL does not already exist, and focused backend route tests.
